definition_en: far below a surface, or to a very great degree
core_image: 一颗石子沉进水里，一直落到看不见的深处
scene: 她把话说得很慢，眼睛看着桌角，像是从很里面取出来的。She was deeply moved by the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 deeply 指「深深地」（第 1 个义项：一直落到内部很深处）；句意是那封信让她深受触动。

senses.title: Far below the surface
senses.definition: at or towards a great distance below a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面以下很深的地方
senses.example: The anchor sank deeply into the soft mud.
senses.exampleCN: 锚深深地陷进软泥里。
senses.why: Depth is measured by how far a thing travels downward.
senses.whyCN: 深度就是看一样东西往下走了多远。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: very much, used with feelings, needs and beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 非常，多与情感、需要和信念连用
senses.example: She was deeply moved by the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她深受触动。
senses.why: A feeling that reaches the bottom of us cannot be called mild.
senses.whyCN: 一直落到心底的感受，就不能算轻微。

senses.title: In a thorough and serious way
senses.definition: in a careful and thorough manner, of thought or study
senses.definitionCN: 在思考或研究上认真而透彻
senses.example: He thought deeply before he gave his answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他深思之后才给出回答。
senses.why: Thinking that goes far down is thinking done well.
senses.whyCN: 想得够深，才算想得够好。

intro.en: Deeply is deep plus the old adverb ending -ly, and deep goes back to an Old English word for a low place.
intro.cn: deeply 是 deep 加古老的副词词尾 -ly；deep 则来自古英语中表示低处的词。

items.en: Deop named the sea and any hollow place that went far down.
items.cn: deop 指大海，也指任何往下很深的凹陷之处。

items.en: The adverb ending -lice was already shortening to -ly.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -lice 当时已经在缩成 -ly。

items.en: Writers used deeply for both sunken things and strong feelings.
items.cn: 作家用它同时写沉下去的东西和强烈的感情。

items.en: Deeply settled into phrases about grief, sleep and debt.
items.cn: 它稳稳进入描写悲伤、睡眠与债务的说法里。

items.en: Today it mostly measures the strength of a feeling or belief.
items.cn: 如今它多半用来衡量情感或信念的强度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deep root, and the meaning group offers stronger adverbs for the same feeling.
note.cn: 形近组共用同一个「深」的根，近义组则给出表示同一种感受的更强副词。

entries.definition: going a long way down from the top
the distance from the top to the bottom
to make or become deeper
in a way that touches the very bottom of feeling
entries.definitionCN: 以触及情感最深处的方式

entries.definition: with very strong force or feeling
entries.definitionCN: 带着极强的力量或情感

entries.definition: very much, often of respect or thanks
entries.definitionCN: 非常，常用于敬意或感谢

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stone dropping into still water and end with a thought that goes all the way down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一颗石子落进静水开始，落到一直想到底的心思。

normal.en: A stone is not loud when it lands; the quiet is how you know it went far.
normal.cn: 石子落水并不响，安静才说明它落得够深。

normal.en: Deep sleep and deep sorrow both take you where no one can follow.
normal.cn: 沉睡与深悲都会把你带到别人跟不进去的地方。

normal.en: When a letter makes your eyes hot, you have been moved deeply.
normal.cn: 一封信让眼睛发热，就是被深深打动了。

normal.en: Roots are never seen; that is why they hold the tree so well.
normal.cn: 根从来看不见，所以才把树抱得那么牢。

normal.en: Add -ly to deep and the depth turns into a manner of doing.
normal.cn: deep 后面加 -ly，深度就变成了一种做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into dark water and not finding the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进暗水里，怎么也摸不到底。

abstract.en: Picture a word spoken so low that the room leans in to hear it.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说得极轻，整间屋子都凑过去听。

abstract.en: Picture roots under grass, wider than the branches above.
abstract.cn: 想象草下的根系，比上面的枝叶还要铺得开。

examples.en: We are deeply grateful for all the help you gave us.
examples.cn: 我们非常感激你给予的全部帮助。

examples.en: The well is deeply cut into the hard rock.
examples.cn: 这口井深深地凿进坚硬的岩石里。

examples.en: She breathed deeply and began to speak.
examples.cn: 她深深吸了一口气，开始讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deeply 记成「底里」：deep 是深，ly 是「地」，一直到底里，就是深深地。

root: deep 源自古英语 deop，本义是「往下的深处」，可指海，也可指任何凹陷。加副词词尾 -ly 之后，deeply 同时继承了具体与抽象两层意思：既指沉在下面，也指情感、信念或思考达到最深处。

sensesIntro.en: From a stone going down, to a heart that is touched, to a mind that thinks it through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗石子往下沉，到一颗心被打动，再到一个念头被想透。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone sinking until the bottom cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子沉下去，直到看不见底。

branches.en: The first sense is simple distance downward, measured in space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是往下的距离，用空间来量。

branches.en: The same downward movement, felt in the chest, becomes strong emotion.
branches.cn: 同样的往下，落到胸口，就成了强烈的情感。

branches.en: Applied to thought, depth means care taken to the end.
branches.cn: 用在思考上，深度就是一直做到最后的认真。

branches.en: Space and feeling share one word because both have a bottom.
branches.cn: 空间与情感共用一个词，因为两者都有底。

branches.en: A strong feeling and a deep thought are both things we do not skim.
branches.cn: 强烈的感受与深刻的思考，都是不能草草掠过的东西。

intro.en: Deeply belongs to the deep family: a verb of deepening, a noun of depth and a set of compounds.
intro.cn: deeply 属于 deep 这一族：有表示加深的动词、表示深度的名词，还有一批复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in deeply; both parts are native English.
latinIntro.cn: deeply 里没有拉丁成分，两个部分都是英语本族语。

items.meaning: in a deep or intense way
items.example: They talked deeply into the night.
items.exampleCN: 他们一直深谈到夜里。

items.example: The lake is deep in the middle.
items.exampleCN: 湖中央很深。

items.example: The river deepens after the bend.
items.exampleCN: 河流转过弯之后变深了。

items.meaning: the measure of how deep something is
items.example: They measured the depth of the pool.
items.exampleCN: 他们量了水池的深度。

items.example: The deepness of his voice filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 他低沉的嗓音充满大厅。

items.meaning: firmly fixed and hard to change
items.example: It is a deep-seated habit.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个根深蒂固的习惯。

items.meaning: long established and hard to remove
items.example: The fear was deep-rooted in the village.
items.exampleCN: 这种恐惧在村里根深蒂固。

items.meaning: found in the far part of the sea
items.example: They study deep-water fish.
items.exampleCN: 他们研究深水鱼类。

definition_en: to win against an opponent, or to make a plan fail; also a loss in a contest
core_image: 对手低下头，慢慢走出场地
scene: 终场哨响，主队球员垂着头走向更衣室，看台上没有一个人说话。The young team defeated the champions by one goal.
sceneCN: 这里 defeat 指「击败」（第 1 个义项：在比赛或争斗中战胜对手）；句意是这支年轻队伍以一球之差战胜了冠军队。

senses.title: Win a contest against someone
senses.definition: to win a victory over an opponent in a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中战胜对手
senses.example: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。
senses.why: A contest ends the moment one side can no longer answer.
senses.whyCN: 比赛在一方再也还不了手的那一刻就结束了。

senses.title: Make a hope or plan fail
senses.definition: to cause a plan, hope or purpose to come to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望或目的无法实现
senses.example: The heavy rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。
senses.why: A plan can be beaten just as a person can be beaten.
senses.whyCN: 计划也会像人一样被打败。

senses.title: A loss in a contest
senses.definition: the fact of losing a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中输掉的事实
senses.example: The defeat left the players silent in the changing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败让球员们在更衣室里一言不发。
senses.why: Every victory leaves behind a second word for the other side.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利，都会给另一方留下另一个词。

intro.en: Defeat came to English through French, but its pieces are Latin: dis- meaning apart and facere meaning to do.
intro.cn: defeat 经法语进入英语，但零件是拉丁的：dis- 表示分开，facere 表示做。

items.en: Disfacere meant to undo or destroy what had been made.
items.cn: disfacere 意为把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉。

items.en: Desfait named the state of being undone.
items.cn: desfait 指被拆散、被毁掉的状态。

items.en: English took the word as a noun for a lost battle.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，作名词指一场打输的仗。

items.en: The verb grew beside the noun and took over the action.
items.cn: 动词在旁边长出来，接过「打败」这个动作。

items.en: A team can defeat a rival, and a problem can defeat a plan.
items.cn: 如今队伍能击败对手，难题也能让计划落空。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the de- opening, and the meaning group moves from beating someone to mastering a difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组都以 de- 开头，近义组则从打赢对手一路走到克服困难。

entries.definition: a fault that makes something imperfect
to protect someone from harm
the act of guarding against attack
to win against someone in a game
to take control of a place by force
entries.definitionCN: 用武力占领并控制某地

entries.definition: to deal with a difficulty successfully

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the whistle at the end of a match and end with a plan that never happened.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从比赛结束的哨声开始，落到一个没能实现的计划。

normal.en: The scoreboard is honest: it says who answered last.
normal.cn: 记分牌最诚实，它只写谁最后还了手。

normal.en: A team can be beaten, and so can a good idea.
normal.cn: 队伍会被打败，好主意也一样。

normal.en: Rain does not argue with a picnic; it simply defeats it.
normal.cn: 大雨不和野餐争论，它直接把野餐毁掉。

normal.en: In defeat a crowd learns the sound of its own silence.
normal.cn: 在失败里，人群听见了自己沉默的声音。

normal.en: Defeat and defend are twins: one takes the field, one guards it.
normal.cn: defeat 和 defend 像双胞胎：一个上场攻，一个守家门。

abstract.en: Picture a flag folded and carried off the field.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被叠好，带离场地。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic basket still packed while rain hits the window.
abstract.cn: 想象雨打着窗，野餐篮还原封未动。

abstract.en: Picture a head lowered just enough to be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头低下去，刚好让人看见。

examples.en: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
examples.cn: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。

examples.en: The rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
examples.cn: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。

examples.en: After the defeat, the coach spoke to each player alone.
examples.cn: 失败之后，教练单独和每个球员谈了话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defeat 记成「敌废」：de 开头像「得」，对手被打得彻底废掉，这一仗就是击败。

root: 来自拉丁语 disfacere，由 dis-（分开）与 facere（做）组成，本义是把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉；经古法语 desfait 进入英语。它先指打输一场仗的结果，十六世纪起动词用法兴盛，后来又引申为让计划、希望落空。

sensesIntro.en: From a rival who cannot answer, to a plan that cannot happen, to the word for losing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从再也还不了手的对手，到无法实现的计划，再到表示输掉的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side walks off the field with a lowered head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一方低着头走出场地。

branches.en: The first sense is a rival who can no longer answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是再也还不了手的对手。

branches.en: The same force applied to a plan leaves it undone.
branches.cn: 同样的力量落到计划上，计划就做不成了。

branches.en: Seen from the other side, the same event is called a loss.
branches.cn: 从另一方看，同一件事就叫失败。

branches.en: One word serves both winner and loser, depending on who speaks.
branches.cn: 同一个词同时给赢家和输家，看是谁在说。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that stopped before it finished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没走完就停下来的事。

intro.en: Defeat grows a small family of nouns about giving up and adjectives about never being beaten.
intro.cn: defeat 长出一小族词：有表示放弃的名词，也有表示不曾被击败的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is facere, to do, with the prefix dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 facere（做），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to win against, or a loss
items.example: They feared defeat more than pain.
items.exampleCN: 他们怕失败胜过怕痛苦。

items.meaning: the habit of expecting to lose
items.example: Defeatism spread through the camp.
items.exampleCN: 失败主义在营地里蔓延。

items.meaning: a person who expects to lose
items.example: He was called a defeatist for doubting the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他因为怀疑计划被人叫作失败主义者。

items.example: The boxer retired undefeated.
items.exampleCN: 这位拳手以不败之身退役。

items.example: No army is undefeatable.
items.exampleCN: 没有哪支军队是无法战胜的。

items.example: Silence proved self-defeating.
items.exampleCN: 沉默反而适得其反。

items.example: The champion looked defeatable that night.
items.exampleCN: 那晚冠军看上去是可以被击败的。

items.meaning: the one who wins against another
items.example: He met his defeater the next season.
items.exampleCN: 下个赛季他遇上了击败过他的人。

definition_en: a fault that makes something imperfect; also to leave one's country or group for another
core_image: 新杯子对着光一转，杯壁上现出一道细纹
scene: 质检员把杯子举到灯下，慢慢转了一圈，忽然停住了手。The inspector found a defect in the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 defect 指「缺陷」（第 1 个义项：产品上的瑕疵）；句意是质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了瑕疵。

senses.title: A fault in a made thing
senses.definition: a small fault that spoils the working of a product
senses.definitionCN: 使产品不能正常使用的小毛病
senses.example: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。
senses.why: A flaw shows itself only when the light is right.
senses.whyCN: 瑕疵只有在光线对的时候才露出来。

senses.title: A weakness in a person or plan
senses.definition: a weakness in character, argument or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 性格、论证或安排上的薄弱之处
senses.example: There is one defect in your argument.
senses.exampleCN: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。
senses.why: What breaks a thing is the same whatever the thing is.
senses.whyCN: 弄坏东西的那个原因，放在哪儿都一样。

senses.title: Leave one side for another
senses.definition: to abandon one's country or group and join the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 离开自己的国家或团体，投向对立一方
senses.example: He defected to the neighbouring country in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 他秘密叛逃到了邻国。
senses.why: A person with a crack in loyalty simply walks away.
senses.whyCN: 忠诚上有了裂缝的人，就抬脚走开了。

intro.en: Defect comes from Latin deficere, to fail or desert, built from de- away and facere to do.
intro.cn: defect 来自拉丁语 deficere（做不好、离开），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）组成。

items.en: Deficere meant to be lacking or to fall away from a duty.
items.cn: deficere 意为缺少，或从职守上退开。

items.en: Defectus named a gap, a failure or a desertion.
items.cn: defectus 指缺口、失误或背离。

items.en: English took it first as a noun for something missing.
items.cn: 英语先把它作名词，指缺失的东西。

items.en: The verb appeared with the sense of deserting a side.
items.cn: 动词用法出现，意思是背弃一方。

items.en: Today a defect is mostly a fault found in goods, plans or eyes.
items.cn: 如今 defect 多指货物、方案或眼睛上的毛病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the defe- opening, and the meaning group names one fault in three ways.
note.cn: 形近组共用 defe- 开头，近义组则用三种说法讲同一种毛病。

entries.definition: to win against an opponent
to protect someone from attack
lacking something needed
a mark or weakness that spoils something
entries.definitionCN: 破坏事物的瑕疵或弱点

entries.definition: a mistake or a bad part in something
a failure to reach a good standard
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到应有水准之处

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crack seen against the light and end with a man quietly changing sides.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从对着光看见的一道裂纹开始，落到一个人悄悄换了阵营。

normal.en: A perfect cup is silent; a cracked one rings differently.
normal.cn: 完好的杯子不出声，裂了的敲起来音不一样。

normal.en: Every argument has one place where it gives way.
normal.cn: 每个论证都有一处会松口的地方。

normal.en: A gap in a wall is small, but that is where the wind comes in.
normal.cn: 墙上的缝不大，风偏偏从那进。

normal.en: A soldier who leaves his post is the same word as a broken part.
normal.cn: 离开岗位的士兵，和坏掉的零件共用一个词。

normal.en: De-fect: something not done, and so not whole.
normal.cn: de-fect 拆开看，就是「没做全」，所以不完整。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line in glass that catches the light for a second.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃里一条细线，只闪了一下光。

abstract.en: Picture a key that almost turns but never quite does.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，差一点就能转动。

abstract.en: Picture a coat left on a chair by someone who is not coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套留在椅子上，主人不再回来。

examples.en: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
examples.cn: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。

examples.en: This model was returned because of a design defect.
examples.cn: 这款因为设计缺陷被退了回来。

examples.en: There is one defect in your argument.
examples.cn: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defect 记成「得废」：de 开头，fect 听着像「废掉」，东西一废，就是有缺陷。

root: 源自拉丁语 deficere（缺少、背离），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）合成，名词 defectus 指缺口与背离。英语先借作名词表示缺失，十六世纪又生出「叛逃」的动词义，两条线都从「离开本该在的位置」长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From a crack in a cup, to a hole in an argument, to a man who walks to the other side.
sensesIntro.cn: 从杯子上的裂纹，到论证里的漏洞，再到走到对面去的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin crack that only shows in the right light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只在合适光线下才显出的细纹。

branches.en: The first sense is a fault inside a finished product.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是成品内部的一处毛病。

branches.en: The same missing piece, in reasoning and in character, is a weakness.
branches.cn: 同样的缺失放到论证和性格上，就是弱点。

branches.en: A person who lacks loyalty simply leaves his own side.
branches.cn: 少了忠诚的人，就直接离开自己这一方。

branches.en: Objects and arguments both fail at the point where something is absent.
branches.cn: 物件和论证都是在缺了一块的地方出问题。

branches.en: Both senses describe a place where the whole can no longer be trusted.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指整体不再可靠的那一处。

intro.en: Defect forms adjectives of being faulty and nouns for the act of deserting.
intro.cn: defect 可派生出表示有毛病的形容词，也有表示背弃的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is facere, to do, with de- meaning away or down.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 facere（做），前缀 de- 表示离开或向下。

items.example: The defect was easy to see.

senses.title: Guarding against attack
senses.definition: the act of protecting a place or person from attack

senses.example: The old wall was built for defence against northern raids.
senses.exampleCN: 这道古墙是为防御北方袭扰而修的。
senses.why: A wall is a promise made before the enemy arrives.
senses.whyCN: 墙是在敌人到来之前就先许下的承诺。

senses.title: The case argued for the accused
senses.definition: the arguments and evidence given for a person in court

senses.title: The forces and works of a country
senses.definition: the armed forces and buildings that protect a country

intro.en: Defence goes back to Latin defendere, to ward off, built from de- away and -fendere to strike.
intro.cn: defence 上溯到拉丁语 defendere（挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）组成。

items.en: Defendere meant to push a blow away from oneself.
items.cn: defendere 意为把打来的一击推开。

items.en: Defense carried the word into the language of law and war.
items.cn: defense 把这个词带进法律与战争的语言。

items.en: English used defence for both a shield and a plea.
items.cn: 英语用它同时指盾牌和申辩。

items.en: Spelling split, with defence in Britain and defense in America.
items.cn: 拼写分成两支，英国用 defence，美国用 defense。

items.en: Defence now also names a whole national system of protection.
items.cn: 如今它还可以指整套国家防护体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defence 记成「挡风死」：de 开头，fence 是篱笆，篱笆挡风又挡人，就是防御。

root: 源自拉丁语 defendere（把打击挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）合成，经古法语 defense 进入英语。它最早兼指盾牌与申辩，十七世纪后英式拼作 defence、美式拼作 defense，如今还引申为整个国家的防务体系。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall that holds, to a voice that answers in court, to a system that guards a country.
sensesIntro.cn: 从守得住的墙，到法庭上应答的声音，再到护卫一国的体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate shut with a shield behind it.

branches.en: The first sense is the physical act of keeping a blow away.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把打击挡在外面的实际动作。

branches.en: The same act in words becomes the case for the accused.
branches.cn: 同样的动作换成言语，就是为被告申辩。

branches.en: Repeated for a whole country, the act becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 为整个国家重复这个动作，它就成了制度。

branches.en: A wall and an army do the same job at different sizes.
branches.cn: 一道墙和一支军队，只是规模不同，做的是同一件事。

branches.en: Shield and argument both stand between a person and harm.
branches.cn: 盾与辩词，都挡在人和伤害之间。

intro.en: Defence gathers verbs, adjectives and nouns about guarding and about speaking up.

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is -fendere, to strike, with de- meaning away.

definition_en: to protect someone or something from attack, or to speak in support of a person or idea
core_image: 一个人挡在门口，把身后的人护住
scene: 球门前的守门员张开双臂，用身体挡住了近角。The keeper defended the near post with his body.
sceneCN: 这里 defend 指「防守」（第 1 个义项：保护位置不受攻击）；句意是守门员用身体守住了近角。

senses.title: Keep someone safe from attack
senses.definition: to protect a person or place from harm or attack
senses.definitionCN: 保护人或地点免受伤害或攻击
senses.example: Two soldiers defended the bridge all night.
senses.exampleCN: 两名士兵整夜守着那座桥。
senses.why: To defend is to put your own body where the blow is going.
senses.whyCN: 保卫就是把自己的身体放到打击落下的地方。

senses.title: Speak up for a person or idea
senses.definition: to argue in support of someone or something that is criticized
senses.definitionCN: 为受到批评的人或事提出支持的理由
senses.example: She defended her decision at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上为自己的决定辩护。
senses.why: Words can stand in front of a person just as a body can.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能像身体一样，站在一个人前面。

senses.title: Hold a position in sport
senses.definition: to try to stop the other side from scoring or from taking a title
senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止对方得分或夺走头衔
senses.example: The champion defended his title in three sets.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军用三盘守住了自己的头衔。
senses.why: A title is a place, and places must be held.
senses.whyCN: 头衔就是一个位置，而位置总要有人守。

intro.en: Defend comes from Latin defendere, to strike away, made of de- away and -fendere to strike.

items.cn: 如今球队守领先优势，作者也维护自己的观点。

branches.en: Shield and argument are the same stance in different material.

branches.en: Both senses are about not giving up what one already has.

intro.en: Defend has a large family of nouns for guards, arguments and the act itself.

definition_en: to state the exact meaning of something, or to mark its limits clearly
core_image: 用一条细线把一片地方圈起来
scene: 老师把粉笔放下，让学生在纸上用一句话说清那个词的意思。The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 define 指「给…下定义」（第 1 个义项：说明词的确切含义）；句意是老师要我们用一句话说清那个词。

senses.title: State the exact meaning
senses.definition: to say exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说出一个词或概念的含义
senses.example: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。
senses.why: A meaning held in the head is not yet shared with anyone.
senses.whyCN: 留在脑子里的意思，还不算和别人共有。

senses.title: Mark the limits of something
senses.definition: to show where the edge or limit of something lies
senses.definitionCN: 指出事物的边缘或限度在哪里

senses.exampleCN: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。

senses.whyCN: 说清一样东西是什么，也就说清了它不是什么。

senses.title: Be the mark of a character
senses.definition: to be the quality that clearly marks a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 成为清楚标示人或事物特点的品质
senses.example: Patience defines a good teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。
senses.why: The line around a thing is what lets us know it again.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西圈起来的那条线，让我们能再认出它。

intro.en: Define comes from Latin definire, to set a boundary, from de- completely and finis end or limit.
intro.cn: define 来自拉丁语 definire（划定界限），由 de-（彻底）与 finis（终点、界限）组成。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary, the end of a field or of a life.
items.cn: finis 指边界，可以是一块田的尽头，也可以是生命的终点。

items.en: Definire meant to draw the line around a thing.
items.cn: definire 意为绕着一件事物画出界线。

items.en: Definir kept the sense of settling and deciding.
items.cn: definir 保留了确定与裁定的意思。

items.en: English used define for explaining words as well as limits.
items.cn: 英语用它既讲界限，也讲词义。

items.en: Today we define terms, borders, duties and even a style.
items.cn: 如今我们定义术语、边界、职责，甚至一种风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fine ending, and the meaning group moves from naming to making plain.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line drawn in the dirt and end with a word that makes a person known.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地上画出的一条线开始，落到一个让人被认出的词。

abstract.en: Picture a name written under a drawing, fixing what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象画下写着一个名字，把画的内容定住。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.

root: 源自拉丁语 definire，由 de-（彻底）与 finis（界限、终点）组成，本义是绕着一块地画出界线；经古法语 definir 进入英语。界线之内是它，界线之外不是它，所以这个词既表示划定范围，也表示说清含义。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a field, to a line around a word, to the line that marks a person.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn around a piece of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细线把一块地围起来。

branches.en: The first sense draws the line around a word's meaning.

branches.en: Laid on a person, the line marks what is most truly his.
branches.cn: 这条线落到人身上，就标出他最真的那一面。

branches.cn: 含义与边界都是靠划出限度做成的。

branches.en: Both senses tell us where something begins and ends.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在告诉我们事物从哪里开始、到哪里为止。

intro.en: Define has given English a whole set of words about clear limits: definition, definite and indefinite.
intro.cn: define 给英语送来一整组关于明确界限的词：definition、definite、indefinite。

definition_en: without any doubt, or in a clear and firm way

senses.exampleCN: 星期六我一定会到。

senses.title: As a warm yes in talk

senses.exampleCN: 当然，我们就坐早班车。

senses.whyCN: 用力说出的赞同，就是一份小小的礼物。

items.exampleCN: 他们看的是高清比赛。

definition_en: a level or amount of something; a unit of measurement; a title given by a university
core_image: 温度计上的刻度，一格一格往上
scene: 炉子上的水开始翻滚，壶嘴喷出白气，窗户蒙上一层雾。Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
sceneCN: 这里 degree 指「度」（第 1 个义项：测量温度的单位）；句意是水在一百度时沸腾。

senses.title: A level or amount
senses.definition: the level or amount of a quality or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 某种性质或感受所处的水平与分量
senses.example: I agree with you to some degree.
senses.exampleCN: 我在某种程度上同意你。
senses.why: Almost nothing is simply yes or no; there are steps between.
senses.whyCN: 很少有事情只是是与非，中间还有一级一级的台阶。

senses.title: A unit on a scale
senses.definition: a unit used to measure temperature, angle or height
senses.definitionCN: 测量温度、角度或高度的单位
senses.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
senses.exampleCN: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。
senses.why: To compare heat or turn, people first had to cut the scale into steps.
senses.whyCN: 要比较冷热或转角，先得把刻度切成格。

senses.title: A title from a university
senses.definition: a rank given by a university to someone who has finished a course
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予完成学业者的等级称号
senses.example: She earned a degree in history last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年拿到了历史学学位。
senses.why: Learning also climbs, and the top of the climb gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 学问也是一步步往上走，走到顶上就该有个名号。

intro.en: Degree goes back to Latin gradus, a step, through Old French degre, a rank on a ladder.
intro.cn: degree 上溯到拉丁语 gradus（台阶），经古法语 degre（梯子上的等级）进入英语。

items.en: Gradus meant a step, a pace or a rung of a ladder.
items.cn: gradus 指一步、一步的距离，或梯子的一级。

items.en: Degre named a rank and a step upward.
items.cn: degre 指等级，也指向上的一级。

items.en: English used it for steps of heat and of honour.
items.cn: 英语用它讲冷热的级差，也讲身份的等级。

items.en: Universities began to award degrees as ranks of learning.
items.cn: 大学开始用学位标示学问的等级。

items.en: The word now measures temperature, angles, feelings and study.
items.cn: 如今它量温度、量角度，也量情感与学问。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gre sound, and the meaning group is made of words for how much of something there is.
note.cn: 形近组共用 gre 这个音，近义组则是几个表示「有多少」的词。

entries.definition: a level of quality or a class in school
entries.definitionCN: 质量等级或学校里的年级

entries.definition: an official order made by a ruler
entries.definitionCN: 统治者发布的正式命令

entries.definition: to lower someone's rank or worth
entries.definitionCN: 降低某人的等级或价值

entries.definition: a height or standard reached
how far something reaches or happens
entries.definitionCN: 某事物延伸或发生的范围

entries.definition: how much there is of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thermometer climbing and end with a name given at the top of the climb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从往上爬的温度计开始，落到爬到顶上领到的那个名号。

normal.en: A ladder is only useful because it has steps.
normal.cn: 梯子之所以有用，就因为有一级一级。

normal.en: Hot and cold are not two things but two ends of one line.
normal.cn: 冷和热不是两样东西，而是一条线的两头。

normal.en: A degree in hand is a step turned into a name.
normal.cn: 手里的学位，就是把一级台阶换成了名号。

normal.en: By degrees is the only way a tree grows.
normal.cn: 树只能一点点长，这就是逐渐。

normal.en: Grade and degree both come from the same step.
normal.cn: grade 与 degree 都是从同一级台阶来的。

abstract.en: Picture a red line rising in a thin glass tube.
abstract.cn: 想象细玻璃管里一条红线往上走。

abstract.en: Picture a rope ladder with a name tied to the top rung.
abstract.cn: 想象一架绳梯，最高一级上系着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a winter room warmed one step at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天的屋子，一格一格暖起来。

examples.en: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
examples.cn: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。

examples.en: I agree with you to some degree.
examples.cn: 我在某种程度上同意你。

examples.en: She earned a degree in history last year.
examples.cn: 她去年拿到了历史学学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 degree 记成「地格瑞」：地上一格一格往上走，每一格就是一个程度。

root: 源自拉丁语 gradus（一步、一级台阶），经古法语 degre 进入英语。台阶既能量冷热，也能量身份与学问：于是它同时表示程度、度数与学位；by degrees 保留了「一级一级走」的老画面。

sensesIntro.en: From a rung on a ladder, to a mark on a scale, to a title at the top of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 从梯子上的一级，到刻度上的一格，再到学问顶端的名号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of marks climbing up a glass tube.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃管上一格一格往上爬的刻度。

branches.en: The first sense is how far along the scale a quality sits.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是某种性质在刻度上走到哪一格。

branches.en: The second sense is the mark itself, used for heat and angle.
branches.cn: 第二个义项就是那一格刻度，量冷热也量角度。

branches.en: Climbed far enough in study, a person receives a rank.
branches.cn: 在学问上爬得够高，人就会得到一个等级。

branches.en: A feeling and a temperature are both read off the same ladder.
branches.cn: 感受与温度，都是沿着同一架梯子读出来的。

branches.en: Both senses turn a smooth climb into countable steps.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把连续的攀升切成可数的格。

intro.en: Degree shares its Latin step with gradual, graduate and degrade, a whole family of climbing words.
intro.cn: degree 与 gradual、graduate、degrade 共用拉丁语「台阶」这个词根，是一整族往上走的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is gradus, a step, from gradi, to walk.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 gradus（台阶），出自 gradi（行走）。

items.example: The temperature rose by ten degrees.
items.exampleCN: 温度上升了十度。

items.example: There was a gradual change in colour.
items.exampleCN: 颜色有逐渐的变化。

items.example: The room gradually grew warm.
items.exampleCN: 屋里渐渐暖和起来。

items.meaning: to finish a course of study
items.example: He will graduate next June.
items.exampleCN: 他明年六月毕业。

items.meaning: a small step or shade of difference
items.example: The sky showed fine gradations of grey.
items.exampleCN: 天空呈现出细腻的灰度层次。

items.example: The chemical degrades in sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 这种化学品在阳光下会分解。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher level
items.example: They upgraded the old system.
items.exampleCN: 他们升级了旧系统。

items.example: By degrees the noise died away.
items.exampleCN: 声音渐渐地消失了。

definition_en: to make something happen later than planned, or the time lost by waiting
core_image: 站台上的人群一起抬头看晚点的牌子
scene: 大雪压住了铁轨，清晨的列车一班接一班停在站外。Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
sceneCN: 这里 delay 指「耽搁」（第 1 个义项：使事情比计划更晚发生）；句意是大雪让早班列车晚点。

senses.title: Make it happen later
senses.definition: to arrange for something to take place at a later time
senses.definitionCN: 把某事安排到更晚的时间进行
senses.example: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。
senses.why: A thing put off is a thing still waiting on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 被推迟的事，就是还搁在架子上等着的。

senses.title: Hold someone up on the way
senses.definition: to make a person or vehicle late by slowing them down
senses.definitionCN: 因拖慢速度而使人或车辆迟到
senses.example: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪让早班列车晚点。
senses.why: One slow point on a road makes every traveller late.
senses.whyCN: 路上一个慢下来的地方，就让所有赶路的人迟到。

senses.title: The time lost in waiting
senses.definition: the period of waiting caused by something being late
senses.definitionCN: 因某事迟到而产生的等待时间
senses.example: There was a delay of two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误了两个小时。
senses.why: Waiting is the shape that lost time takes in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 等待，就是失去的时间在心里留下的形状。

intro.en: Delay comes from Old French delaier, to put off, built on Latin laxare, to loosen.
intro.cn: delay 来自古法语 delaier（往后放），底层是拉丁语 laxare（放松、松开）。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen a hold or a rope.
items.cn: laxare 意为把抓住的手或绳子松开。

items.en: Delaier joined de- with laier, to leave something for later.
items.cn: delaier 由 de- 与 laier 合成，意为留到以后再说。

items.en: English used delay for both putting off and being held up.
items.cn: 英语用它既指主动推迟，也指被动耽搁。

items.en: The noun delay settled into talk of journeys and courts.
items.cn: 名词用法在旅途与法庭的说法里安定下来。

items.en: Trains, flights and replies are all said to be delayed.
items.cn: 如今列车、航班和回复都可以说被延误。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ay ending, and the meaning group names three ways of making something wait.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ay 这个尾巴，近义组则是三种让人或事等一等的方式。

entries.definition: to pass a message or signal on
to be slowly destroyed by natural causes
to make a fear or worry less strong
to move an event to a later date
entries.definitionCN: 把活动改到更晚的日期

entries.definition: to decide to do something later
to stop something from moving on time

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crowd looking up at a board and end with two hours that simply vanished.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一群人抬头看牌子开始，落到凭空消失的两个小时。

normal.en: A train is late once, but the waiting is repeated by everyone.
normal.cn: 列车只晚一次，等待却被每个人各经历一遍。

normal.en: Delay is not a stop; the wheels are still turning, only slower.
normal.cn: 耽搁不是停下，轮子还在转，只是慢了。

normal.en: The meeting moved by two days costs two days of guessing.
normal.cn: 会议挪两天，就多出两天猜测。

normal.en: To delay a reply is to say nothing in a loud way.
normal.cn: 拖着不回，就是用很响的方式什么也不说。

normal.en: Relay passes a message on; delay keeps it back.
normal.cn: relay 把消息传下去，delay 把消息留住。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with one hand moving slower than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，一根针走得比另一根慢。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that does not move but grows.
abstract.cn: 想象一支不往前挪、却越来越长的队伍。

abstract.en: Picture a letter left in a drawer for a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信在抽屉里躺了一星期。

examples.en: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
examples.cn: 大雪让早班列车晚点。

examples.en: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
examples.cn: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。

examples.en: There was a delay of two hours.
examples.cn: 延误了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delay 记成「地雷」：路上踩到地雷，队伍就走不动，只好延误。

root: 来自古法语 delaier（留到以后），其底层是拉丁语 laxare（松开），本义是把抓着的事放开、让它往后滑。它先指主动推迟，后来也指被动耽搁，如今连列车、航班与回复晚到都用它。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan moved forward on the calendar, to a train held in the snow, to the empty hours that remain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从日历上往后挪的计划，到被雪挡住的列车，再到剩下那几个空掉的小时。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station board where one line turns late.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站牌上有一行变成了晚点。

branches.en: The first sense moves the agreed time further on.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把商定的时间往后挪。

branches.en: The second sense is being slowed on the way.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是在路上被拖慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the waiting that results.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是由此产生的等待。

branches.en: A choice and an accident produce the same lateness.
branches.cn: 主动的选择与被动的意外，造成同一种晚。

branches.en: The train and the empty hour are one event seen twice.
branches.cn: 晚点的列车与空掉的一小时，是同一件事的两面。

intro.en: Delay forms a few adjectives and nouns, all about lateness and waiting.
intro.cn: delay 能派生出几个形容词与名词，全都与晚点和等待有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is laxare, to loosen, with de- giving the sense of away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 laxare（松开），前缀 de- 带来「离开」的意味。

items.meaning: to put off, or the wait
items.example: The delay was caused by fog.
items.exampleCN: 延误是雾造成的。

items.example: The delayed train arrived at noon.
items.exampleCN: 晚点的列车中午才到。

items.example: A delaying tactic bought them a day.
items.exampleCN: 拖延的办法为他们争到一天。

items.example: The parcel arrived undelayed.
items.exampleCN: 包裹准时到了。

items.example: He was the delayer of every plan.
items.exampleCN: 每个计划都是他拖下来的。

items.example: Please answer without delay.
items.exampleCN: 请立即回复。

items.example: A long delay tested our patience.
items.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了我们的耐性。

items.meaning: a gap between act and result
items.example: There is a short time delay in the signal.
items.exampleCN: 信号有很短的延迟。

definition_en: a person sent to speak for a group; also to give a task or power to someone else
core_image: 一个人举起写着团体名字的牌子
scene: 会议开始前，每个人在门口的册子上写下自己的名字和所代表的城市。Each delegate signed the book at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 delegate 指「代表」（第 1 个义项：替团体出席的人）；句意是每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。

senses.title: A person who speaks for a group
senses.definition: someone chosen to attend a meeting and act for a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 被选去参加会议并代表较大团体行事的人
senses.example: Each delegate signed the book at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。
senses.why: A crowd cannot all stand at one table, so it sends one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 一群人没法都坐到同一张桌前，只好派出一双手。

senses.title: Hand a task to someone
senses.definition: to give part of one's work to another person to do
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的一部分工作交给别人去做
senses.example: A good manager delegates the small tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 好的管理者会把小事分派出去。
senses.why: Two hands can hold more than one pair can.
senses.whyCN: 两双手能拿的东西，比一双手多。

senses.title: Give power to another
senses.definition: to give someone the right to act or decide in your place
senses.definitionCN: 授予他人代替你行事或决定的权力
senses.example: The board delegated full power to the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会把全部权力授予了新主管。
senses.why: Trust is a key that changes hands without changing locks.
senses.whyCN: 信任是一把换了手、却没换锁的钥匙。

intro.en: Delegate comes from Latin delegare, to send with a charge, from de- away and legare to send.
intro.cn: delegate 来自拉丁语 delegare（派人带任务去），由 de-（离开）与 legare（派遣）组成。

items.en: Legare meant to send a person with a duty.
items.cn: legare 意为派一个人带着任务去。

items.en: Delegare added the idea of handing the charge over.
items.cn: delegare 又多了一层「把任务交出去」的意思。

items.en: English used delegate as a noun for a sent person.
items.cn: 英语先把 delegate 作名词，指被派出去的人。

items.en: The verb grew, meaning to entrust work or power.
items.cn: 动词用法长出来，指托付工作或权力。

items.en: Managers now delegate tasks as easily as states send delegates.
items.cn: 如今管理者分派任务，就像国家派出代表一样自然。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the leg stem, and the meaning group names the person who stands in for others.
note.cn: 形近组共用 leg 词干，近义组则是几个「替别人出面」的人。

entries.definition: a group sent to speak for others
entries.definitionCN: 被派去代表他人发言的一群人

entries.definition: done on purpose and after thought
an official messenger of high rank
a person chosen to act for a group
entries.definitionCN: 被选来代表团体行事的人

entries.definition: a person who acts for a leader
a person sent to carry a message

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a name written at a meeting door and end with a key handed to someone you trust.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从会议门口写下的名字开始，落到交到信任之人手里的钥匙。

normal.en: One person at the table can carry a whole town in a folder.
normal.cn: 桌边一个人，文件夹里能装下一整座城。

normal.en: A manager who keeps every task ends up holding nothing well.
normal.cn: 什么活都攥在手里的管理者，最后什么也拿不稳。

normal.en: To delegate is to lend your signature for a while.
normal.cn: 授权，就是把自己的签名借出去一阵。

normal.en: A delegate is a voice sent away from home.
normal.cn: 代表，是从家里被派出去的一个声音。

normal.en: Legare means to send, so a delegate is one who was sent.
normal.cn: legare 是派遣，所以代表就是被派出去的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised with a card bearing a town's name.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起来，牌子上写着一座城的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of papers moving from one desk to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠纸从一张桌子移到另一张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a key pressed into a palm and the fingers closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙按进掌心，手指合拢。

examples.en: Each delegate signed the book at the door.
examples.cn: 每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。

examples.en: A good manager delegates the small tasks.
examples.cn: 好的管理者会把小事分派出去。

examples.en: The board delegated full power to the new director.
examples.cn: 董事会把全部权力授予了新主管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delegate 记成「得力干将」：de 开头，legate 是派出去的人，派出去的总是得力的那位。

root: 源自拉丁语 delegare，由 de-（离开）与 legare（派遣）合成，本义是派人带着任务出去。英语先把它作名词表示使者与代表，十六世纪又生出动词义，指把工作或权力托付给别人。

sensesIntro.en: From a person sent to a meeting, to a task handed over, to the right to decide in your place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被派去开会的人，到交出去的一项工作，再到代你决定的权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair of hands holding a card for many people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手替许多人举着一块牌子。

branches.en: The first sense is the chosen person who speaks for the rest.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被选中替众人说话的人。

branches.en: The second sense is work passed to another pair of hands.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把工作交到另一双手里。

branches.en: The third sense lends the right to decide, not only the work.
branches.cn: 第三个义项借出的是决定权，不只是活儿。

branches.en: A representative and a handed task are both things sent outward.
branches.cn: 代表与被交出的任务，都是被送出去的东西。

branches.en: Both senses trust another person with a part of your own role.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把自己角色的一部分托付给别人。

intro.en: Delegate brings nouns of groups and of the act of handing power over.
intro.cn: delegate 带来表示团体和授权行为的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is legare, to send, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 legare（派遣），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.example: One delegate spoke for the village.
items.exampleCN: 一位代表为村子发言。

items.meaning: a group sent, or the act of entrusting
items.example: A small delegation met the mayor.
items.exampleCN: 一个小代表团见了市长。

items.example: The delegated work was finished early.
items.exampleCN: 分派出去的工作提前完成了。

items.meaning: the one who hands work over
items.example: The delegator keeps the final say.
items.exampleCN: 委派者保留最后决定权。

items.meaning: able to be handed to another
items.example: Not every duty is delegable.
items.exampleCN: 并非每项职责都能交出去。

items.meaning: a person sent to discuss trade
items.example: The trade delegate met the exporters.
items.exampleCN: 贸易代表会见了出口商。

items.example: Good leaders delegate authority.
items.exampleCN: 好的领导者会下放权力。

items.meaning: a person attending a conference for a group
items.example: Every conference delegate got a badge.
items.exampleCN: 每位会议代表都领到了胸牌。

definition_en: to remove written or stored material completely
core_image: 一行字在屏幕上闪了一下，然后整行消失
scene: 她按住退格键不放，整整一段文字飞快地缩短，最后只剩光标。She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
sceneCN: 这里 delete 指「删除」（第 1 个义项：把文字或文件彻底去掉）；句意是她一键删掉了整段文字。

senses.title: Remove a file or a line
senses.definition: to remove a file, message or line of text from a device
senses.definitionCN: 把文件、信息或文字行从设备上去掉
senses.example: She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
senses.exampleCN: 她一键删掉了整段文字。
senses.why: What is gone from the screen is gone from the argument too.
senses.whyCN: 从屏幕上消失的东西，也从论证里消失了。

senses.title: Strike a word out of a text
senses.definition: to take out a word or passage from a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 从一篇文字里去掉某个词或一段话
senses.example: The editor deleted two long sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了两个长句。
senses.why: Writing is choosing what the reader will never see.
senses.whyCN: 写作就是决定哪些东西读者永远看不到。

senses.title: Wipe out a record
senses.definition: to destroy stored information so it cannot be found
senses.definitionCN: 销毁存储的信息，使人再也找不到
senses.example: He deleted the old records from the system.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧记录从系统里清除了。
senses.why: A memory kept in a machine can be taken away at once.
senses.whyCN: 存在机器里的记忆，可以一下子被拿走。

intro.en: Delete comes from Latin delere, to blot out, whose printer's mark dele told a reader to take a letter away.
intro.cn: delete 来自拉丁语 delere（抹去），印刷用的符号 dele 就是叫读者把字去掉。

items.en: Delere meant to wipe a surface clean of marks.
items.cn: delere 意为把表面上的痕迹擦干净。

items.en: The command dele was written on proofs to mean remove.
items.cn: 校样上写 dele，就是要求删掉。

items.en: English printers borrowed dele as a mark of deletion.
items.cn: 英国印刷工借来 dele，作为删除的记号。

items.en: The verb delete spread to any removal of writing.
items.cn: 动词 delete 扩展到一切去掉文字的行为。

items.en: Computers gave it a key of its own and a new home.
items.cn: 计算机给了它一个专属按键和新的家。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dele- opening, and the meaning group moves from taking out to rubbing away.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dele- 开头，近义组则从取出走到擦去。

entries.definition: a person sent to speak for a group
entries.definitionCN: 被派去代表团体发言的人

entries.definition: easily broken or needing care
entries.definitionCN: 容易破碎或需要小心对待的

entries.definition: to use up most of a supply
to take something away from its place
to rub out marks completely
to take a part away from the whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line vanishing from a screen and end with a record that no longer exists.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从屏幕上消失的一行字开始，落到一份已经不存在的记录。

normal.en: A deleted sentence leaves no echo, only a shorter page.
normal.cn: 删掉的句子没有回声，只留下一张更短的纸。

normal.en: The editor's pencil is a small knife with good manners.
normal.cn: 编辑的铅笔，是一把有礼貌的小刀。

normal.en: Backspace is quicker than regret and much cheaper.
normal.cn: 退格键比后悔快得多，也便宜得多。

normal.en: A file deleted is a room with the door painted over.
normal.cn: 被删的文件，是一间把门刷平了的屋子。

normal.en: Dele was a mark on paper before it was a key on a board.
normal.cn: dele 先是纸上的记号，后来才成了键盘上的键。

abstract.en: Picture a line of letters breaking into small square pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字母碎成一个个小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing one key and stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指按下一个键，然后停住。

abstract.en: Picture a name gone from a list, and the space still clean.
abstract.cn: 想象名单上少了一个名字，留下的地方很干净。

examples.en: She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
examples.cn: 她一键删掉了整段文字。

examples.en: The editor deleted two long sentences.
examples.cn: 编辑删去了两个长句。

examples.en: He deleted the old records from the system.
examples.cn: 他把旧记录从系统里清除了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delete 记成「得离题」：写离题的话，就该被删掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 delere（抹去、销毁），印刷时代用 dele 这个符号要求删字，后来才成为动词。它的核心一直是「把痕迹从表面上弄掉」，进入计算机时代后，删除文件与记录都沿用了这个老词。

sensesIntro.en: From a paragraph gone, to a word cut out, to a record wiped clean.
sensesIntro.cn: 从消失的一段文字，到被剪掉的一个词，再到被清空的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of text that stops existing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一行字突然不再存在。

branches.en: The first sense is a file or line removed from a device.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把文件或文字行从设备上去掉。

branches.en: The second sense cuts a passage out of a text.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是从文章中剪去一段。

branches.en: The third sense clears stored memory away.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把存储的记忆清空。

branches.en: Screen and page both lose something at a keystroke.
branches.cn: 屏幕与纸页都在一按之间少了点什么。

branches.en: Both senses leave a clean place where something stood.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在原处留下干净的一块。

intro.en: Delete gives English nouns of removal and a modern verb for bringing back what was removed.
intro.cn: delete 给英语送来表示删除的名词，以及一个把删掉内容恢复的现代动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delere, to blot out, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delere（抹掉），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: Delete the last line.
items.exampleCN: 把最后一行删掉。

items.example: The deletion left a small gap.
items.exampleCN: 删掉的地方留下一个小空档。

items.example: The deleted file was not missed.
items.exampleCN: 被删掉的文件没人想起。

items.example: The comment is deletable by the owner.
items.exampleCN: 这条评论可由本人删除。

items.meaning: to bring back a removed file
items.example: He undeleted the letter by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 他误操作把那封信恢复了。

items.meaning: a sign showing text should go
items.example: The deletion mark sat in the margin.
items.exampleCN: 删除记号留在页边。

items.example: Accidental deletion lost the whole folder.
items.exampleCN: 误删把整个文件夹弄丢了。

items.example: She pressed the delete key twice.
items.exampleCN: 她按了两次删除键。

definition_zh: 故意的；从容的；仔细考虑
definition_en: done on purpose after thinking; slow and calm; also to think something over carefully
core_image: 一双手把两样东西放在天平两端慢慢比较
scene: 十二个人在屋里坐了很久，桌上的纸翻了又翻，谁也没有先开口。The jury deliberated for three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 deliberate 指「仔细考虑」（第 3 个义项：反复权衡后作出判断）；句意是陪审团商议了三个小时。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: planned and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有计划有意图的，而非偶然发生的
senses.example: The mistake was not deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误不是故意的。
senses.why: What is weighed before it is done leaves a mark of choice.
senses.whyCN: 做之前先称量过的事，会留下选择的痕迹。

senses.title: Slow and unhurried
senses.definition: moving or speaking slowly and in a calm, steady way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或说话缓慢、平稳而不慌
senses.example: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。
senses.why: A person who is thinking does not want to arrive too soon.
senses.whyCN: 正在思考的人，不想太早到达。

senses.title: Weigh a matter in council
senses.definition: to discuss and think about a question carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前就一个问题仔细讨论与思考
senses.example: The jury deliberated for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团商议了三个小时。
senses.why: Two sides of a question are two pans that must be let settle.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题有两面，就像天平的两个盘，要让它慢慢稳下来。

intro.en: Deliberate comes from Latin deliberare, to weigh well, from de- and libra, a balance.
intro.cn: deliberate 来自拉丁语 deliberare（好好称量），由 de- 与 libra（天平）组成。

items.en: Libra was the scale on which goods were weighed.
items.cn: libra 是称货用的天平。

items.en: Deliberare meant to hold a question in the balance.
items.cn: deliberare 意为把一个问题放到天平上称。

items.en: English took the verb for thinking a matter over.
items.cn: 英语借来这个动词，表示反复思量一件事。

items.en: The adjective added the sense of a calm, slow manner.
items.cn: 形容词用法又添了从容、缓慢的意味。

items.en: Today a deliberate act is one nobody can call careless.
items.cn: 如今一个故意的行为，就是谁也不能说它粗心。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from intended to unhurried.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从有意一路走到不慌不忙。

entries.definition: long and careful discussion
needing gentle and careful handling
a person sent to act for a group
done because one means to do it
thought out before it happens
entries.definitionCN: 在发生之前就已想好的

entries.definition: moving without any rush

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two pans of a balance and end with steps that never hurry.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从天平的两个盘开始，落到从不着急的脚步。

normal.en: A choice that was weighed has a different weight in the hand.
normal.cn: 称过的选择，拿在手里的分量不一样。

normal.en: A slow walk across a room says more than a quick word.
normal.cn: 慢慢走过一间屋子，比一句快话更能说明问题。

normal.en: Twelve people in one room are twelve balances, all waiting.
normal.cn: 一屋十二个人，就是十二架天平，一起等着。

normal.en: An accident leaves no plan behind; a deliberate act does.
normal.cn: 意外不留计划，故意的行为会留下。

normal.en: Libra is a balance, so to deliberate is to let the pans settle.
normal.cn: libra 是天平，所以商议就是让两个盘慢慢稳下来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a scale perfectly level.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把天平端得平平的。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed down heel first, then toe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚先落脚跟，再落脚尖。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs and one sheet of paper moving between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，一张纸在中间传来传去。

examples.en: The jury deliberated for three hours.
examples.cn: 陪审团商议了三个小时。

examples.en: The mistake was not deliberate.
examples.cn: 这个错误不是故意的。

examples.en: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
examples.cn: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliberate 记成「地里拨来拨去」：先掂量再动手，就是反复考虑；掂量过的举动，就是故意的。

root: 源自拉丁语 deliberare，词根 libra 是称货用的天平，本义是把一个问题放到天平上称一称。称量要慢，所以它既指「反复考虑」，也指考虑过后有意的举动，还引申出不慌不忙的姿态。

sensesIntro.en: From a question held in a balance, to a choice made with open eyes, to a walk that refuses to hurry.
sensesIntro.cn: 从放在天平上的问题，到睁着眼作出的选择，再到不肯着急的脚步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of a balance slowly coming level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平的两个盘慢慢平下来。

branches.en: The first sense is an act that came out of a choice.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是从选择里长出来的行为。

branches.en: The second sense keeps the slow pace of weighing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项保留了称量时那种慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the weighing itself, done aloud in a group.
branches.cn: 第三个义项就是称量本身，在一群人里说出来。

branches.en: A purpose and a discussion are the two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 目的与商议，是同一个过程的两头。

branches.en: Both senses treat time as something worth spending.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把时间当成值得花的东西。

intro.en: Deliberate has a family of adverbs and nouns about thinking before acting.
intro.cn: deliberate 有一族副词与名词，都与「先想再做」有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is libra, a balance, with de- giving a sense of thoroughness.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 libra（天平），前缀 de- 带来彻底的意味。

items.example: It was a deliberate choice.
items.exampleCN: 那是一个有意的选择。

items.example: She deliberately left the door open.
items.exampleCN: 她故意让门开着。

items.example: After long deliberation they agreed.
items.exampleCN: 商议很久之后他们同意了。

items.example: The council is a deliberative body.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会是审议机构。

items.example: The deliberateness of the act was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个行为的有意十分明显。

items.example: They deliberated on the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们就这个计划进行了商议。

items.example: The work went on at deliberate speed.
items.exampleCN: 工作以从容的速度推进。

items.example: It was a deliberate attempt to mislead.
items.exampleCN: 那是蓄意误导。

definition_en: on purpose, or in a slow and calm way
core_image: 一只手慢慢伸出去，明知会碰倒仍不收回
scene: 他把最后一道题空着交上去，走出考场时脚步很稳。He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
sceneCN: 这里 deliberately 指「故意地」（第 1 个义项：有意识地这么做）；句意是他故意把最后一题留空。

senses.title: With full intention
senses.definition: with the full knowledge that one is doing it
senses.definitionCN: 完全知道自己正在这么做
senses.example: He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
senses.exampleCN: 他故意把最后一题留空。
senses.why: A hand that does not shake shows the mind has already decided.
senses.whyCN: 手不发抖，说明心里早就定了。

senses.title: Without any hurry
senses.definition: in a slow, steady and calm manner
senses.definitionCN: 以缓慢、平稳而镇定的方式
senses.example: She closed the book deliberately and stood up.
senses.exampleCN: 她不慌不忙地合上书，站起身来。
senses.why: Slowness can be a form of control, not a lack of it.
senses.whyCN: 慢也可以是一种掌控，而不是失控。

intro.en: Deliberately is deliberate plus -ly, and deliberate goes back to Latin libra, a balance.
intro.cn: deliberately 是 deliberate 加 -ly，而 deliberate 上溯到拉丁语的 libra（天平）。

items.en: Libra was the scale used to weigh goods.
items.cn: libra 是称货用的天平。

items.en: Deliberare meant to weigh a matter before acting.
items.cn: deliberare 意为行动前先把事情称一称。

items.en: English kept the picture of a slow and careful mind.
items.cn: 英语保留了那种缓慢而小心的画面。

items.en: The adverb marked acts that were clearly intended.
items.cn: 副词形式用来标示明显有意的行为。

items.en: Today it can accuse and admire in the same breath.
items.cn: 如今它既可用于指责，也可用于赞赏。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deliberate stem, and the meaning group offers three ways to say it was no accident.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deliberate 这个词干，近义组则给出三种「不是意外」的说法。

entries.definition: done on purpose and after thought
long and careful discussion
in a gentle and careful way
with the purpose of doing it
for a set reason, not by chance
entries.definitionCN: 出于既定理由，而非偶然

entries.definition: while fully aware of what one does
entries.definitionCN: 完全清楚自己在做什么

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a blank answer on a test paper and end with a hand that closes a book slowly.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从考卷上一处空白开始，落到一只慢慢合上书的手。

normal.en: A blank left on purpose is still an answer.
normal.cn: 有意留出的空白，也是一种回答。

normal.en: The steadiest hand in the room has already decided.
normal.cn: 屋里最稳的那只手，早就做好了决定。

normal.en: To be vague on purpose is to hide behind fog you made.
normal.cn: 故意含糊，就是躲进自己造的雾里。

normal.en: Slow steps are not weak steps.
normal.cn: 慢的脚步，不是弱的脚步。

normal.en: Deliberate plus -ly turns a weighing mind into a manner.
normal.cn: deliberate 加 -ly，称量的心思就变成了举止。

abstract.en: Picture a pen lifted just before it touches the paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在碰到纸之前停住。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open for no one in particular.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被扶着，谁也没在过。

abstract.en: Picture two eyes meeting yours and not looking away.
abstract.cn: 想象一双眼睛对上你的，没有躲开。

examples.en: He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
examples.cn: 他故意把最后一题留空。

examples.en: She closed the book deliberately and stood up.
examples.cn: 她不慌不忙地合上书，站起身来。

examples.en: The report was deliberately vague about the date.
examples.cn: 报告在日期上故意写得含糊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliberately 记成「地里有谱」：心里早有谱，才做得不慌不忙，也都是故意为之。

root: 由 deliberate 加副词词尾 -ly 构成。deliberate 出自拉丁语 deliberare，词根 libra 是天平，本义是称量、权衡。称过的举动是有意的，称的过程是缓慢的，所以这个词同时表示「故意地」与「从容地」。

sensesIntro.en: From an act nobody can call accidental, to a pace nobody can call hurried.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没人能说是意外的举动，到没人能说是匆忙的步调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand that does not stop itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只稳稳伸出、并不收回的手。

branches.en: The first sense removes any excuse of accident.
branches.cn: 第一个义项排除了「不小心」这个借口。

branches.en: The second sense is the same control shown in speed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同样的掌控体现在速度上。

branches.en: Both senses come from a mind that has already weighed the matter.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出自一颗已经称量过的心。

branches.en: Deliberately in a charge sheet means the act was chosen.
branches.cn: 在指控里说故意，意思是这行为是选出来的。

branches.en: In praise, deliberately means nothing was rushed or wasted.
branches.cn: 在称赞里，它意味着没有一样东西被赶出来或浪费掉。

intro.en: Deliberately sits at the adverb end of the deliberate family, next to deliberation and deliberative.
intro.cn: deliberately 站在 deliberate 这一族的副词一端，旁边是 deliberation 与 deliberative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is libra, a balance, with de- meaning thoroughly.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 libra（天平），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: He deliberately took the longer road.
items.exampleCN: 他故意走了更远的那条路。

items.example: Her move was deliberate.
items.exampleCN: 她那一动是有意的。

items.example: The deliberation lasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 商议持续了一小时。

items.example: They met in a deliberative mood.
items.exampleCN: 他们带着审议的心情开会。

items.example: The deliberateness of the silence was plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片沉默显然是有意的。

items.example: His answer was deliberately vague.
items.exampleCN: 他的回答故意含糊。

items.example: The train ran deliberately slow.
items.exampleCN: 列车故意开得很慢。

items.example: The letter was deliberately ignored.
items.exampleCN: 那封信被故意搁着不理。

definition_en: easily broken or harmed; finely made; needing careful handling
core_image: 薄胎瓷碗托在掌心，手指不敢用力
scene: 她托着那只薄薄的杯子，走路时连呼吸都放轻了。She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
sceneCN: 这里 delicate 指「易碎的」（第 1 个义项：容易碰坏）；句意是她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

senses.title: Easily broken or hurt
senses.definition: thin or weak enough to be damaged with little force
senses.definitionCN: 薄或弱到稍一用力就会损坏
senses.example: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
senses.exampleCN: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。
senses.why: What is lovely is often what breaks first.
senses.whyCN: 好看的东西，往往最先坏。

senses.title: Finely made and pleasing
senses.definition: made with fine skill and a light, careful touch
senses.definitionCN: 以精细手艺和轻巧手法做成
senses.example: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。
senses.why: Thin lines take longer to cut, and the eye knows it.
senses.whyCN: 细线要花更久去刻，眼睛看得出这份工夫。

senses.title: Needing careful handling
senses.definition: sensitive and easy to upset, of a matter or situation
senses.definitionCN: 指事情或处境敏感，容易被打乱
senses.example: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
senses.exampleCN: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。
senses.why: Some things are held together by almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西，几乎只靠一点点力气才没有散。

intro.en: Delicate comes from Latin delicatus, which first meant giving pleasure and then finely made.
intro.cn: delicate 来自拉丁语 delicatus，先指令人愉悦，再指做得精细。

items.en: Delicatus described something that delighted the senses.
items.cn: delicatus 形容让感官愉悦的东西。

items.en: Over time it came to mean fine, soft and easily harmed.
items.cn: 后来它又指纤细、柔软、容易受损。

items.en: English used it for fine cloth, food and health.
items.cn: 英语用它形容精细的布、食物和身体。

items.en: The word moved from the body to matters of feeling and politics.
items.cn: 这个词从身体一路挪到情感与政治。

items.en: A delicate matter is one handled with words instead of hands.
items.cn: 如今微妙的事，要用言语而不是手去托。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from breakable to fine to tricky.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从易碎走到精细再到棘手。

entries.definition: to give time or effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力献给某个目的

entries.definition: a person sent to act for a group
a rare and pleasing food
easily broken
very thin or made with great skill
not obvious and needing care to notice
entries.definitionCN: 不明显、需要细心才能察觉的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thin cup in two hands and end with two countries standing very still.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从双手托着的一只薄杯开始，落到两个一动不动站着的国家。

normal.en: The thinner the cup, the more the hand must listen.
normal.cn: 杯子越薄，手越要会听。

normal.en: Fine lines are slow lines, and the eye pays for them.
normal.cn: 细线都是慢线，眼睛是愿意为此付钱的。

normal.en: A flower proves nothing about strength, only about care.
normal.cn: 花不证明力量，只证明有人肯小心。

normal.en: A delicate balance is not a balance that stays by itself.
normal.cn: 微妙的平衡，不是自己会保持的平衡。

normal.en: Delicacy of taste and delicacy of skin share one skin-thin idea.
normal.cn: 口味的细腻与皮肤的娇嫩，共享同一个「薄」的念头。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip moving a hair off a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖把一根头发从纸上捻走。

abstract.en: Picture lace held up against a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一片蕾丝举在窗前。

abstract.en: Picture two glass balls touching and neither breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象两个玻璃球轻轻相触，谁也没碎。

examples.en: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
examples.cn: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

examples.en: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
examples.cn: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。

examples.en: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
examples.cn: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delicate 记成「得立刻特小心」：薄得一碰就坏，所以得立刻特别小心。

root: 源自拉丁语 delicatus，本义是令人愉悦、讨人喜欢，后来添上纤细、柔软、容易受损的意思。经法语进入英语后，它从布料、食物与身体，一路扩展到情感与局势，于是易碎、精致、微妙三层意思并存。

sensesIntro.en: From a cup that breaks, to work that took great skill, to a balance nobody dares disturb.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一碰就碎的杯子，到极费手艺的活计，再到谁也不敢碰的平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin-walled cup held in two careful hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手小心托着一只薄壁杯子。

branches.en: The first sense is thinness that breaks under little force.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是稍一用力就坏的薄。

branches.en: The second sense is thinness used as skill and beauty.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把薄做成了手艺与美。

branches.en: The third sense is thinness in a situation, where one word can tip it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是处境的薄，一句话就能打破。

branches.en: What is finely made is also what needs care to keep.
branches.cn: 做得精细的东西，也需要小心才留得住。

branches.en: Both senses praise a thing that cannot be handled roughly.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说：这东西经不起粗手粗脚。

intro.en: Delicate has nouns and adverbs about fineness, and the noun delicacy carries both taste and care.
intro.cn: delicate 有表示精细的名词与副词，其中 delicacy 既有美味，也有分寸。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delicatus, pleasing and fine, from deliciae, delight.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delicatus（悦人而精细），出自 deliciae（愉悦）。

items.example: The glass is very delicate.
items.exampleCN: 这只玻璃杯非常薄脆。

items.example: She held the leaf delicately.
items.exampleCN: 她轻轻捏着那片叶子。

items.meaning: a rare food, or fineness of touch
items.example: The fish is a local delicacy.
items.exampleCN: 这种鱼是当地的美味。

items.example: The delicateness of the bowl surprised me.
items.exampleCN: 这碗的薄让我吃惊。

items.example: The lake keeps a delicate balance.
items.exampleCN: 这片湖维持着微妙的平衡。

items.example: Money is a delicate issue here.
items.exampleCN: 钱在这里是个敏感话题。

items.example: The baby has delicate skin.
items.exampleCN: 婴儿的皮肤很娇嫩。

items.example: The tea has a delicate taste.
items.exampleCN: 这茶味道清雅。

definition_en: tasting or smelling very good; also pleasing in a surprising way
core_image: 刚出炉的面包被掰开，热气一下子涌到脸上
scene: 面包刚出炉，她掰下一角，还没吃就笑了。The kitchen smelled delicious when the bread came out.
sceneCN: 这里 delicious 指「美味的」（第 1 个义项：吃起来或闻起来很好）；句意是面包一出炉，厨房里就香气扑鼻。

senses.title: Very good to eat
senses.definition: having a taste or smell that gives great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 味道或气味让人非常愉悦
senses.example: The kitchen smelled delicious when the bread came out.
senses.exampleCN: 面包一出炉，厨房里就香气扑鼻。
senses.why: Taste is the one sense that answers before words do.
senses.whyCN: 味道是最先给出答案、来不及用词的那种感觉。

senses.title: Pleasing in an unexpected way
senses.definition: giving pleasure to the mind, especially something witty
senses.definitionCN: 让心里受用，尤指带巧思的事物
senses.example: There was a delicious irony in his words.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话里有一种耐人寻味的讽刺。
senses.why: The mouth is not the only place where pleasure is tasted.
senses.whyCN: 能尝到滋味的地方，不只嘴巴。

intro.en: Delicious comes from Latin deliciosus, full of delight, from deliciae, a delight.
intro.cn: delicious 来自拉丁语 deliciosus（充满愉悦），出自 deliciae（乐趣）。

items.en: Deliciae meant delight, often of the senses.
items.cn: deliciae 指愉悦，常指感官上的享受。

items.en: Deliciosus described what gave that pleasure.
items.cn: deliciosus 形容带来这种愉悦的东西。

items.en: Delicious carried the word toward food and charm.
items.cn: delicious 一路把这个词带向食物与魅力。

items.en: English used it mostly at the table at first.
items.cn: 英语最初多在餐桌上用它。

items.en: Now a line in a play can be called delicious too.
items.cn: 如今戏里的一句台词也可以说「够味」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -cious sound, and the meaning group is made of words for food that pleases.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -cious 这个音，近义组则是几个形容食物讨喜的词。

entries.definition: easily broken or finely made
confused and seeing things, often from illness
entries.definitionCN: 常因病而神志不清、看见幻象的

entries.definition: of great value
having a good strong flavour
looking or smelling good enough to eat
entries.definitionCN: 看着或闻着就让人想吃的

entries.definition: very pleasing in any way
entries.definitionCN: 在任何方面都令人愉快的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with warm bread torn open and end with a clever line that tastes of irony.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从掰开的热面包开始，落到一句尝得出讽刺的巧话。

normal.en: Smell reaches the kitchen door before the bread does.
normal.cn: 香味总比面包先到厨房门口。

normal.en: A good meal ends conversation for a moment, and that is praise.
normal.cn: 好吃的一餐会让谈话停一下，这一停就是夸奖。

normal.en: The same word serves soup and sarcasm.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能形容汤，也能形容讽刺。

normal.en: Delicious is delight with a spoon in it.
normal.cn: delicious 就是插着一把勺子的愉悦。

normal.en: A cake that looks delicious has already started eating you.
normal.cn: 看着就馋的蛋糕，其实先把你吃了一口。

abstract.en: Picture steam curling up from a torn loaf.
abstract.cn: 想象掰开的面包上冒起一缕热气。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon stopped halfway to a mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子停在嘴边。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that appears before the first bite.
abstract.cn: 想象第一口还没吃，笑先出来了。

examples.en: The kitchen smelled delicious when the bread came out.
examples.cn: 面包一出炉，厨房里就香气扑鼻。

examples.en: That was the most delicious soup I have had all year.
examples.cn: 那是我这一年喝过最好喝的汤。

examples.en: There was a delicious irony in his words.
examples.cn: 他的话里有一种耐人寻味的讽刺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delicious 记成「地里热死」：地里刚收的东西热腾腾上桌，好吃得让人忘了热。

root: 源自拉丁语 deliciosus，出自 deliciae（愉悦、乐趣），本义是「带来愉悦的」。经古法语进入英语后，它先在餐桌上站稳，指味道极好，后来又引申到言辞与巧思，凡让人心里受用的都可说 delicious。

sensesIntro.en: From bread that fills the kitchen with steam, to a line that fills the mind with pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让厨房满是热气的面包，到让心里一亮的句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm steam rising from freshly torn bread.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚掰开的面包上腾起热气。

branches.en: The first sense belongs to the tongue and the nose.
branches.cn: 第一个义项属于舌头和鼻子。

branches.en: The second sense hands the same pleasure to the mind.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同样的愉悦交给脑子。

branches.en: Food and wit both give a pleasure that needs no argument.
branches.cn: 食物与巧思都给出一种不必争辩的愉悦。

branches.en: At table the word is simple praise and needs nothing more.
branches.cn: 在餐桌上，这个词就是单纯的称赞。

branches.en: In writing it adds a smile to something sharp.
branches.cn: 在文章里，它给尖锐的东西添了一点笑。

intro.en: Delicious has a small family: an adverb of pleasure, a noun of taste and a compound of looks.
intro.cn: delicious 的家族不大：有表示愉悦的副词、表示美味的名词，还有一个讲卖相的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is deliciae, delight, with the adjective ending -ous.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 deliciae（愉悦），加上形容词词尾 -ous。

items.example: The pie was delicious.
items.exampleCN: 这个派很好吃。

items.example: The room smelled deliciously of coffee.
items.exampleCN: 屋里一股好闻的咖啡香。

items.example: The deliciousness of the soup surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这汤的好喝让我们意外。

items.example: A delicious-looking plate arrived.
items.exampleCN: 端上来一盘看着就馋的菜。

items.meaning: a meal that tastes very good
items.example: We had a delicious meal by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 我们在海边吃了一顿好饭。

items.example: A delicious smell came from the oven.
items.exampleCN: 烤箱里飘出好闻的香味。

items.example: The delay had a delicious irony.
items.exampleCN: 这次延误有一种耐人寻味的讽刺。

items.example: The little cakes were absolutely delicious.
items.exampleCN: 这些小蛋糕极其美味。

definition_en: great pleasure; something that gives pleasure; to give someone great pleasure
core_image: 孩子看见第一场雪，原地跳了起来
scene: 雪刚落下薄薄一层，孩子们冲到院子里，笑声撞在墙上。The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
sceneCN: 这里 delight 指「欣喜」（第 1 个义项：极大的愉快）；句意是初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

senses.title: A rush of great pleasure
senses.definition: a strong feeling of happiness and enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而明亮的快乐感受
senses.example: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。
senses.why: Joy that arrives suddenly comes out as a sound, not a word.
senses.whyCN: 突然到来的快乐，是先从声音里出来的，不是从词里。

senses.title: Something that gives joy
senses.definition: a person or thing that brings great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带来极大快乐的人或事物
senses.example: The garden is her greatest delight.
senses.exampleCN: 花园是她最大的乐趣。
senses.why: We name the source with the same word as the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 我们把源头和感受，用同一个词来叫。

senses.title: Give someone joy
senses.definition: to please someone greatly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人非常高兴
senses.example: The small band delighted the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。
senses.why: A pleasure that can be given away doubles itself.
senses.whyCN: 能送出去的快乐，会变成两份。

intro.en: Delight comes from Latin delectare, to charm, through Old French delit, which English respelled with gh.
intro.cn: delight 来自拉丁语 delectare（使着迷），经古法语 delit 进入英语，后来才拼上 gh。

items.en: Delectare meant to draw someone in with charm.
items.cn: delectare 意为用魅力把人吸引过来。

items.en: Delectatio named the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦。

items.en: Delit kept the sense of a sweet enjoyment.
items.cn: delit 保留了甜美享受的意思。

items.en: English writers added gh, perhaps by confusion with light.
items.cn: 英语写作者加上 gh，可能是受了 light 的影响。

items.en: The word now covers both the feeling and its cause.
items.cn: 如今它既指感受，也指引起感受的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the light ending, and the meaning group moves from joy to the act of pleasing.
note.cn: 形近组绕着 light 这个尾巴，近义组则从快乐走到使人快乐。

entries.definition: very pleasing
the natural light of the sun
very good to eat
a deep feeling of happiness
a feeling of being pleased
to make someone happy

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with children in the first snow and end with a small band making a hall smile.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从初雪里的孩子开始，落到让整座大厅都笑起来的小乐队。

normal.en: The first snow is not a thing but a reason to shout.
normal.cn: 初雪不是一样东西，而是一个喊出来的理由。

normal.en: A garden can be a friend you water.
normal.cn: 一座花园，可以是你浇过水的朋友。

normal.en: What you take delight in, you will find time for.
normal.cn: 你以之为乐的事，总能腾出时间。

normal.en: To delight others is to hand them a small holiday.
normal.cn: 让别人高兴，就是递给对方一个小小的假日。

normal.en: Someone put gh into delight to make it look like light.
normal.cn: 有人往 delight 里塞进 gh，让它看着像 light。

abstract.en: Picture a boot making the first mark in fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子在新雪上踩出第一个印。

abstract.en: Picture a face that cannot stop smiling at nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张对着空气也止不住笑的脸。

abstract.en: Picture hands clapping before the song has ended.
abstract.cn: 想象歌还没唱完，掌声就起来了。

examples.en: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
examples.cn: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

examples.en: The garden is her greatest delight.
examples.cn: 花园是她最大的乐趣。

examples.en: The small band delighted the whole hall.
examples.cn: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delight 记成「地来特」：好事落到地上来，心里一下亮起来，就是欣喜。

root: 源自拉丁语 delectare（以魅力吸引），名词 delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦；经古法语 delit 进入英语，拼写上加了 gh，可能受了 light 的影响。它同时保留了感受、来源与动作三层意思：欣喜、乐事、使高兴。

sensesIntro.en: From a shout in the snow, to the garden that caused it, to the band that caused the shout.
sensesIntro.cn: 从雪地里的一声喊，到引起这声喊的花园，再到让全场喊起来的那支乐队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child jumping in the first snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在初雪里蹦起来。

branches.en: The first sense is the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那种被抬起来的感受。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that lifted it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把心抬起来的那样东西。

branches.en: The third sense is doing that lifting for someone else.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是替别人把心抬起来。

branches.en: Feeling and cause are one word because they arrive together.
branches.cn: 感受与原因共用一个词，因为它们总是一起到。

branches.en: What delights us can be passed on to others.
branches.cn: 让我们高兴的东西，也可以传给旁人。

intro.en: Delight grows adjectives of joy and adverbs of charm, all from the same Latin root.
intro.cn: delight 长出表示高兴的形容词与表示迷人的副词，都出自同一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delectare, to charm, from lacere, to lure.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delectare（使着迷），出自 lacere（引诱）。

items.example: Her face was full of delight.
items.exampleCN: 她满脸欣喜。

items.example: We are delighted to hear the news.
items.exampleCN: 听到这个消息我们很高兴。

items.example: It was a delightful evening.
items.exampleCN: 那是个愉快的夜晚。

items.example: The room was delightfully cool.
items.exampleCN: 屋里凉快得很舒服。

items.example: The delightfulness of the place stayed with us.
items.exampleCN: 那地方的可爱一直留在我们心里。

items.example: She delights in small jokes.
items.exampleCN: 她喜欢小笑话。

items.example: He takes delight in cooking.
items.exampleCN: 他从做饭里得到乐趣。

items.example: To our delight, the sun came out.
items.exampleCN: 让我们高兴的是，太阳出来了。

definition_en: to take goods or letters to a place; to give a speech; to do what was promised
core_image: 一双手把包裹递到门口，收件人签下名字
scene: 快递员在午前按响门铃，把纸箱放在门垫上。The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 deliver 指「递送」（第 1 个义项：把物品送到某处）；句意是司机在中午前把包裹送到了。

senses.title: Take something to its place
senses.definition: to carry goods, letters or food to the person or place waiting for them
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到等待的人或地点
senses.example: The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在中午前把包裹送到了。
senses.why: A thing only counts as sent when it has arrived.
senses.whyCN: 东西只有到了，才算真的寄出去。

senses.title: Give a speech aloud
senses.definition: to speak words to an audience in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合向听众讲出一段话
senses.example: She delivered a short speech at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口作了一个简短的讲话。
senses.why: Words too are carried from one mouth to many ears.
senses.whyCN: 话也是被从一个嘴里送到许多只耳朵里的。

senses.title: Do what was promised
senses.definition: to produce the result that was promised or expected
senses.definitionCN: 交出所承诺或所期待的结果
senses.example: The new team delivered results in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新团队在第一个月就交出了成果。
senses.why: A promise is only a parcel that has not arrived yet.
senses.whyCN: 承诺不过是一个还没送到的包裹。

intro.en: Deliver comes from Old French delivrer, from Latin de- and liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: deliver 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语的 de- 与 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to set a person free.
items.cn: liberare 意为把人释放、使之自由。

items.en: Delivrer added the sense of handing something over.
items.cn: delivrer 又添上「把东西交出去」的意思。

items.en: English used deliver for freeing and for giving up a thing.
items.cn: 英语用它既表示解救，也表示交出东西。

items.en: The sense of carrying goods to a place grew strong.
items.cn: 把货物送到某地的意思渐渐占了上风。

items.en: One can now deliver a parcel, a speech or a result.
items.cn: 如今可以送包裹、作演讲，也可以交出成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver stem, and the meaning group moves from handing over to sending.
note.cn: 形近组共用 liver 这个词干，近义组则从交给一路走到送出。

a result that must be handed over
to live through something again in memory

to cause something to go to a place

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a bell at the door and end with a promise that finally turns into a result.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一声铃开始，落到一个终于变成结果的承诺。

normal.en: A parcel in the van is still only a plan.
normal.cn: 车里的包裹，还只是一个计划。

normal.en: The last step of any journey is a pair of hands.
normal.cn: 任何一段路，最后一步都是一双手。

normal.en: A speech is carried across the room by breath.
normal.cn: 演讲是靠一口气送到屋子对面的。

normal.en: Results are promises that have arrived.
normal.cn: 成果，就是已经送到的承诺。

normal.en: Deliver once meant to set free; now it means to hand over.
normal.cn: deliver 曾表示「使自由」，如今表示「交到手里」。

abstract.en: Picture a box set down on a mat and a pen offered.
abstract.cn: 想象一个箱子放在门垫上，旁边递来一支笔。

abstract.en: Picture one voice going out and many faces lifting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音出去，许多张脸抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture a signed paper slid across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签好的纸从桌面上推过来。

examples.en: The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
examples.cn: 司机在中午前把包裹送到了。

examples.en: She delivered a short speech at the door.
examples.cn: 她在门口作了一个简短的讲话。

examples.en: The new team delivered results in the first month.
examples.cn: 新团队在第一个月就交出了成果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliver 记成「递礼物」：de 开头，liver 听着像「礼物」，把礼物递到手上，就是送达。

root: 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语 liberare（使自由），所以它最早表示「解救、释放」。后来「把东西放出去」变成「把东西交出去」，十五世纪起「送到某地」成为主要意思，又引申出发表演讲与兑现成果。

sensesIntro.en: From a parcel at the door, to words crossing a room, to a promise turned into fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 从门口的包裹，到穿过屋子的话，再到变成事实的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing a parcel into other hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把包裹交到另一双手里。

branches.en: The first sense is a parcel arriving where it was sent.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是包裹到达它被寄去的地方。

branches.en: The second sense carries words instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个义项送的是话，不是货。

branches.en: The third sense carries a result that was owed.
branches.cn: 第三个义项送的是欠着的成果。

branches.en: A parcel and a promise both count only when they arrive.
branches.cn: 包裹与承诺，都要到了才算数。

branches.en: Both senses turn something held back into something handed over.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把攥着的东西变成交出去的东西。

intro.en: Deliver has a family of nouns for the act and the person, and an adjective for what never arrived.
intro.cn: deliver 有表示行为与人的名词，也有表示没送到的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is liberare, to free, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 liberare（使自由），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.meaning: to carry to a place, or to hand over
items.example: They deliver bread every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们每天早上送面包。

items.example: The delivery arrived late.
items.exampleCN: 送货来晚了。

items.example: The deliverer left the box at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 送货人把箱子放在门口。

items.meaning: a result to be handed over
items.example: Each stage has one deliverable.
items.exampleCN: 每个阶段都有一项应交付的成果。

items.example: The letter came back undelivered.
items.exampleCN: 那封信没送到，被退了回来。

items.example: He delivered a speech on peace.
items.exampleCN: 他发表了关于和平的演讲。

items.example: The plan must deliver results soon.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划必须尽快交出成果。

items.example: They delivered on their promise.
items.exampleCN: 他们兑现了承诺。

definition_en: the act of bringing goods or letters; the way words are spoken; the birth of a baby
core_image: 门口的纸箱上贴着一张写着他名字的条子
scene: 巷口的小店在玻璃上贴了一张纸，说是本城范围内不收运费。The shop offers free delivery within the city.
sceneCN: 这里 delivery 指「投递」（第 1 个义项：把货物送到顾客手中）；句意是这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。

pos.zh: 投递；交付；演讲方式；分娩

senses.title: The bringing of goods
senses.definition: the act of taking goods, letters or food to a customer
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到顾客手中的行为
senses.example: The shop offers free delivery within the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。
senses.why: The last metre of a journey is the one the buyer pays for.
senses.whyCN: 一段路的最后一米，才是买家真正花钱买的那段。

senses.title: The way words are spoken
senses.definition: the manner in which a speech or song is given to listeners
senses.definitionCN: 把讲话或歌曲呈现给听众的方式
senses.example: Her delivery was calm and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的表达从容而清楚。
senses.why: The same sentence can be handed over gently or dropped.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话，可以轻轻递过去，也可以扔过去。

senses.title: The birth of a child
senses.definition: the act of a baby coming out of its mother's body
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿从母亲身体里出来的过程
senses.example: The delivery went well and both were healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 分娩顺利，母子都健康。
senses.why: A new life also has to be carried out into the air.
senses.whyCN: 新的生命，也要被送到空气里来。

intro.en: Delivery is deliver plus -y, and deliver goes back to Latin liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: delivery 是 deliver 加 -y，而 deliver 上溯到拉丁语 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to release a person from a hold.
items.cn: liberare 意为把一个人从束缚中放开。

items.en: Delivrer meant to hand over or to set free.
items.cn: delivrer 意为交出，也意为释放。

items.en: The noun delivery named both rescue and handing over.
items.cn: 名词 delivery 同时指解救与交出。

items.en: Trade gave it the everyday sense of goods arriving.
items.cn: 商业给了它「货物送达」这个日常意思。

items.en: It now also covers the manner of speaking and the birth of a child.
items.cn: 如今它也指说话的方式与婴儿的出生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver shape, and the meaning group names what arrives at a door.
note.cn: 形近组共用 liver 这个形状，近义组则指送到门口的那批东西。

normal.en: A promise and a parcel both end at a door.

sensesIntro.en: From a box at the door, to a voice in a hall, to a new life carried into the air.

core.cn: 核心意象：一个箱子放下，上面写着名字。

branches.en: The first sense ends with goods in the buyer's hands.
branches.cn: 第一个义项以货物到买家手中结束。

branches.en: The second sense hands words to listeners instead.
branches.cn: 第二个义项递出去的是话，给的是听众。

branches.en: The third sense is a body arriving into the world.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个身体来到世上。

branches.en: Goods and words are both judged by how they arrive.
branches.cn: 货物与话，都要看它们是怎么到的。

branches.en: Both senses need care at the moment of handing over.
branches.cn: 两个义项在交出的那一刻都需要小心。

intro.en: Delivery sits at the noun end of a family that includes deliver, deliverer and deliverable.
intro.cn: delivery 站在这一族的名词一端，同族还有 deliver、deliverer、deliverable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is liberare, to free, with de- meaning away.
